moments.title: The architects ask Picasso
moments.text: The architects of the new Civic Center commissioned a sculpture for its plaza. Richard Bennett, one of them, wrote Picasso a poem asking him to take it on.

moments.title: Unveiled to a crowd of about 50,000
moments.text: U.S. Steel's American Bridge Company built the 50-foot sculpture in Gary, Indiana, from Picasso's model, and it was unveiled on the plaza. Picasso turned down a $100,000 fee, saying he wanted it to be a gift to the city; some in the crowd carried signs mocking it.

moments.title: Fifty years on
moments.text: The city marked the sculpture's 50th birthday with events including a reenactment of the unveiling.

moments.title: Today: Daley Plaza
moments.text: The untitled sculpture still stands in Daley Plaza in front of the Richard J. Daley Center, formerly the Civic Center.

checked.notes: Unveiled Aug 15, 1967; 50 ft, 162 short tons, Cor-Ten steel, fabricated by American Bridge in Gary (Wikipedia, Chicago Landmarks). Crowd of about 50,000 (WBEZ). Picasso refused $100,000 (Wikipedia). The Afghan hound reading in the old story was not found in the sources checked; they list a woman, a horse or a baboon, so the story was changed. 2017 reenactment per Chicagoist and The Architect's Newspaper coverage. The fabrication year was not confirmed, so it is folded into the unveiling.
